title: PenEngine reads never see a half-applied edit from the pen thread
body:
## Summary
PenEngine had no lock while the TV applied pen messages on the socket thread and read doc, counts and undoAt on the frame loop and heartbeat, so a read could copy a list mid-write and hand the renderer a null.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:61 (doc getter, before) copies `committed` and `livePoints` with no synchronisation; core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:81 (accept, before) mutates them. tv-app calls accept from the pen receive loop (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:63 -> Session.edit) and reads doc from the frame loop (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:184 publishIfDirty) and the heartbeat (Session.heartbeatInput). ArrayList.removeAt and clear() shrink size before nulling the slot, so a concurrent toArray copies a null. Registry concurrency-guards (race-catalog-with-two-histories): the interleaving was neither guarded nor declared legal. Fixed: every public member of PenEngine is @Synchronized; nothing inside calls out, so there is no lock order to violate.

## Flow
- the phone streams a stroke and presses undo while the TV renders at 30 Hz
- Session.edit runs engine.accept on the socket thread; publishIfDirty reads engine.doc on the main thread
- before: a doc with a null annotation or a stroke with a null point reaches the overlay; after: every read sees a whole edit

## Expected impact
The TV overlay and heartbeat stop being able to read a torn document (a null point is an NPE in the renderer). Uncontended monitor cost per call; nothing calls out under the lock.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a reader on another thread never sees a half-applied edit
Before: 20651 torn reads in 2740260 reads over 2 s (PenEngineThreadsTest, writer vs reader)
After: 0 torn reads over the same 2 s run
Method: gate - core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngineThreadsTest.kt red before the lock, green after; :core:test exit 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:61 (before) `val doc: AnnotationDoc get() { val live = liveMeta?.copy(points = livePoints.toList()) ...` (no lock)
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:63 `is PenEffect.Deliver -> session.accept(effect.message)` (socket thread)
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:184 `session.publishIfDirty()` (frame loop -> engine.doc)
red run: torn reads in 2740260 reads; first error: null ==> expected: <0> but was: <20651>

title: The wrong-PIN guess limit holds across LAN connections
body:
## Summary
Only the relay's shared conversation limited wrong PINs; a LAN connection was hung up after one wrong PIN and a guesser simply opened the next, so all 9000 four-digit PINs could be tried at connection speed.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:120 (before) rejected a wrong PIN and closed, keeping no count; MAX_WRONG_PINS / COOLDOWN_MS applied only in sharedHello (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:161). The class comment argued the hang-up limits guessing, but a connection is free, and newest-pen-wins (PenConversation.pair) hands a successful guesser the viewer's pen. Registry device-pairing / timing-defenses: the refusal must throttle the guess budget. Fixed: the count and cooldown live on PairingDesk, shared by every connection to one TV; the desk clock is the latest open or tick. Same constants, same reason strings, already in LinkState.PIN_REFUSALS and the TV card.

## Flow
- a LAN client opens a WebSocket and sends hello with PIN 1000, is refused and closed
- it reconnects with 1001, 1002, ...
- before: every guess is answered, the right one pairs and takes over the pen; after: the sixth hello within 30 s is refused with "too many wrong PINs", the right PIN included

## Expected impact
A neighbour on the Wi-Fi can no longer brute-force the pen in minutes. A viewer who mistypes five times waits 30 s, as on the relay already; a LAN neighbour can now hold that lockout (see the registry-conformance card).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - online PIN guessing over LAN is limited like the relay
Before: every PIN 1000..9999 on a fresh connection within one window: 1 paired, 8999 answered "wrong PIN"
After: 0 paired, 5 answered "wrong PIN", the rest "too many wrong PINs" (PairingGuessLimitTest case 3)
Method: gate - core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PairingGuessLimitTest.kt, cases 1 and 3 red before, green after; shared cases 5b/5c and the dedicated GUARD unchanged
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:120 (before) `if (msg.pin != desk.pin) return reject("wrong PIN")`
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:72 (before) "Because nothing closes, guessing is limited instead" - shared only
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:78 `val pin: String = (1000..9999).random().toString()`
red run case 3: the guesser paired within one cooldown window ==> expected: <0> but was: <1>

title: A short point or shape end is dropped, not thrown on the pen thread
body:
## Summary
A pen point or shape end with fewer than two coordinates decoded fine and then threw IndexOutOfBounds inside PenEngine on the pen receive loop, ending the LAN connection or the relay socket.

## Description
pts, from and to are plain List<Double> (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:25, :32), so [0.5] or [] passes decodePenMessage. PenEngine.handlePen indexed it[0], it[1] and handleShape called metric.distance(from, to). The throw runs inside PenSessionHost.host's receiveLoop (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:106), so it ends the connection; on the relay it ends the shared socket (RelayTransport runCatching -> backoff), unpairing the pen. Registry error-handling / error-doors: a frame that decodes but cannot be drawn should leave by the same door as one that does not decode (dropped). Fixed: short points are skipped, the rest of the batch kept; a shape with a short end is dropped.

## Flow
- a paired pen sends {"type":"shape","tool":"circle","from":[0.5],"to":[0.6,0.5]}
- PenConversation delivers it; Session.edit -> PenEngine.accept
- before: IndexOutOfBounds escapes the receive loop and the connection ends; after: the shape is dropped and the next message draws

## Expected impact
A malformed frame from any pen (a bug, an older client, a hand-written test) no longer drops the connection. Nothing a well-formed client sends changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a malformed geometry frame cannot end the pen connection
Before: 9 of 9 malformed frames (arrow, circle, spotlight x 2 ends, pen points) threw IndexOutOfBounds
After: 0 of 9 throw; a pen batch with one bad point keeps its 3 good points
Method: gate - core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/MalformedGeometryTest.kt red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:159 (before) `val xyp = msg.pts.map { listOf(it[0], it[1], ...) }`
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:194 (before) `radius = metric.distance(msg.from, msg.to)` with from=[0.5]
red run: Caused by: java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException at MalformedGeometryTest.kt:21 / :31 / :46

title: A tap with the arrow or circle tool draws nothing
body:
## Summary
"A tap is not a drawing" was enforced for freehand strokes but not for shapes, so a tap with the arrow or circle tool committed a zero-length arrow (a stray arrowhead) or a radius-0 ring (a dot).

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:182 drops a stroke under two points; handleShape (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:189) committed whatever arrived. The companion sends a shape on every pointerup (companion/index.html endStroke) even when the finger never moved. The TV draws the arrowhead at atan2(0,0) (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:104) and a ring of radius 0 as a dot; the annotation takes an undo slot and adds a drawn moment to the phone's scrub bar. Fixed: arrows and rings shorter than Smoothing.MIN_POINT_DISTANCE are dropped; the spotlight keeps its 0.03 floor on purpose.

## Flow
- the viewer picks Arrow and taps the pad
- the page sends shape from == to
- before: an arrowhead appears on the TV, Undo lights up, a tick appears on the scrub bar; after: nothing is committed

## Expected impact
Taps with the shape tools stop leaving debris and phantom undo steps and moments. A deliberate drag of 0.004 of the width or more draws as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a tap with a shape tool leaves no annotation, undo step or moment
Before: 3 taps -> 3 annotations, canUndo true, 1 moment
After: 3 taps -> 0 annotations, canUndo false, 0 moments; 0.01 drags and a spotlight tap still draw (GUARD)
Method: gate - core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/ShapeTapTest.kt red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:182 `// A tap with under two points is not a stroke; drop it rather than draw a dot.`
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:189 handleShape had no such rule
red run: ShapeTapTest case 1 expected: <0> but was: <3>

title: The phone wire contract is read off the companion page, not a copied list
body:
## Summary
The only test of what the phone sends was five JSON strings typed into PenToolsTest; it covered 5 of the 10 message types the page sends and 1 of its 5 transport commands, and nothing checked the review-mode constants the page copies.

## Description
core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenToolsTest.kt:358 ("every tool the phone can send") is a hand-maintained list (scan-sweep 4.7): it reads its own copy, not the phone. companion/index.html sends hello, pen, shape, erase, tag, undo, redo, clearFrame, clear, transport (toggle, step, jump, rate, seek) and copies MOMENT_SPAN_MS / ON_MOMENT_LEAD_MS from core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Timeline.kt:41. Hold.parse falls back to Default silently, so a renamed hold would throw nowhere. Registry ipc-contract / drift-gates. Built: core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/CompanionContractTest.kt extracts every sent type, cmd, shape tool, pen phase, hold name and the constants from the comment-stripped page and checks each against PenMessage serial names, TransportPlan, PenEngine, Hold and AnnotationTimeline.

## Flow
- someone renames a transport command or a constant on one side
- before: every test stays green and the phone button silently does nothing on the TV
- after: CompanionContractTest names the drifted value

## Expected impact
The protocol between the two contexts that ship separately (the APK copies the page at build) gets a drift gate. Test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - page/TV protocol drift is caught by :core:test
Before: message types checked against the real page 0/10 (5/10 via a copied list); transport cmds 0/5; constants 0/2
After: 10/10, 5/5, 2/2; seeded page (cmd jmp, tool spot, MOMENT_SPAN_MS 600) -> 3 of 5 cases red, restored -> green
Method: gate - seeded control on the page, then restored; :core:test exit 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenToolsTest.kt:359-365 five literal JSON strings (tag, erase, redo, pen, transport step)
companion/index.html:220 `const MOMENT_SPAN_MS = 500, ON_MOMENT_LEAD_MS = 40;` (copy of core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Timeline.kt:41,44)
seeded red: [jmp], [spot], expected: <500> but was: <600>

title: core:test reruns when the companion page changes
body:
## Summary
CompanionContractTest reads companion/index.html, which was not an input of :core:test, so an edit to the page alone left the task UP-TO-DATE and the contract unread.

## Description
core/build.gradle.kts declared no test inputs beyond the module's own sources. Gradle's up-to-date check and build cache therefore skipped :core:test after a page-only edit. Fixed: the page is a declared input (relative path sensitivity). Coupled path: core/build.gradle.kts, required for the contract test to be a gate.

## Flow
- edit companion/index.html only
- run ./gradlew.bat :core:test
- before: UP-TO-DATE, 0 tests; after: the task executes and re-reads the page

## Expected impact
The page contract is checked on exactly the change it guards. One extra file hash per build.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the contract gate sees its input
Before: page-only edit -> :core:test UP-TO-DATE, 0 tests run
After: page-only edit -> :core:test executed, 112 tests run
Method: gate - two :core:test runs around a page-only edit, before and after the input declaration
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
g8 run (page edited, before): BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1s, 0 PASSED lines
g10 run (page edited, after): > Task :core:test (executed), 112 PASSED

title: Frame-stepping refreshes the phone thumbnail on 1 step in 5
body:
## Summary
Heartbeat sends a new paused thumbnail once per 200 ms bucket of t, but a frame step is 40 ms, so four of every five steps leave the phone showing the old frame while the viewer aims.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:290 Heartbeat.beat keys thumbnails on `input.t / THUMB_BUCKET_MS` (200); TransportPlan.FRAME_MS is 40 (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt:21). Stepping 5000, 5040, 5080, 5120, 5160 yields one thumbnail (5000); 5200 the next. The comment says "only once per frame the viewer stops on" - the code says once per five frames. HeartbeatTest case 7 pins the 200 ms bucket. Fix candidate: key on t / FRAME_MS (one thumbnail per stepped frame). Trade-off: up to 5x thumbnails while stepping, each a JPEG data URL on the pen's connection.

## Flow
- pause, press Frame > four times
- the TV moves 40 ms per press; the heartbeat sends no new thumbnail until t crosses a 200 ms boundary
- the phone pad shows the frame from up to 160 ms earlier

## Expected impact
The viewer aims at the frame the TV shows. Could worsen pen round-trip while stepping; that is what the A/B must measure.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the pad shows the frame the TV is paused on after each step
Before: 1 thumbnail per 5 single-frame steps (walked through Heartbeat.beat)
After: 5 per 5 predicted with a 40 ms key; thumbnail bytes while stepping up to 5x
Method: simulation - five steps walked through Heartbeat.beat; the device cost (bytes, round-trip under stepping) needs the Stick
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:290 `val thumbKey = if (input.paused) input.t / THUMB_BUCKET_MS else Long.MIN_VALUE` (THUMB_BUCKET_MS = 200L at :320)
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt:21 `const val FRAME_MS = 40L`
core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversationTest.kt case 7 asserts 5150 -> no thumbnail
instrument: HeartbeatTest stepping case (5 steps -> thumbnails emitted) plus tools/live-ui-test.mjs frame-step journey on the Stick reporting thumbnail bytes and pen round-trip p95 while stepping, both arms

title: A superseded pen is never told it was replaced
body:
## Summary
When a newer pen pairs, the older one stands down silently: its messages are dropped and its heartbeat stops, but nothing tells the phone, which keeps a green dot and a frozen status while its strokes go nowhere.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:166 onText returns emptyList() when `desk.generation != generation`; tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:126 ends pushState when the pen is not current. The superseded phone (companion/index.html) has no state for this: paired stays true, the dot stays green, the last status stays up. Fix candidate: on the first message from a superseded pen, answer Welcome(accepted=false, reason="another pen took over") (+ Close on a dedicated connection), and give the page copy for it that does not invite a PIN ping-pong. Touches the wire behaviour seen by the companion and the copy; product call on whether the old pen may take back.

## Flow
- phone A pairs and draws; phone B pairs with the same PIN
- A keeps drawing
- A's ink echoes locally and vanishes; A's status freezes; nothing explains

## Expected impact
Two people sharing a TV learn who holds the pen. Risk: a reason string the TV card might show (LinkState.PIN_REFUSALS must not include it).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a replaced pen says so instead of failing silently
Before: superseded pen: 0 messages from the TV, dot green, strokes dropped (PenConversationTest case 4 pins the silence)
After: predicted: one refusal with a reason, dot red, pad blocked (the unpaired state 9e1da19b already built)
Method: simulation - walked through PenConversation case 4 and the page; no core test pins the new reply yet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:166 `if (desk.generation != generation) return emptyList()`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:126 `while (isActive && pen.isCurrent)`
core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversationTest.kt case 4 "the older one stands down silently"
instrument: PenConversationTest case: the superseded pen's next message yields a refusal with the new reason; companion-refusal-test case: that reason turns the dot red and blocks the pad

title: The context map omits LinkState.kt and its test
body:
## Summary
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt and core/src/test/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkStateTest.kt are in pen-core's package and depend on PenConversation's reasons, but no context in context-map.json lists them, so no sweep owns them.

## Description
pen-core's file_paths list 12 main files; LinkState.kt (95 lines, the pairing-card reducer, decision-bearing) is the 13th in the same directory and is absent from every context (grep of context-map.json: 0 hits). LinkState.PIN_REFUSALS is the TV-side half of the refusal-reason pair; LinkStateTest ties it to PenConversation (well). A file no context owns is never swept and never in a write set.

## Flow
- grep LinkState context-map.json -> 0 hits
- ls core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core -> 13 files, 12 mapped

## Expected impact
The pairing card's reducer gets an owner. Editing the context map is the director's and the operator's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - every core file has a sweep owner
Before: 2 core files (LinkState.kt, LinkStateTest.kt) in no context
After: 0 once added to pen-core's file_paths
Method: probe - grep of context-map.json against ls of core/src
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
$ grep -n LinkState context-map.json -> (no output)
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:84 `val PIN_REFUSALS: Set<String> = setOf("wrong PIN", "too many wrong PINs")`
escalation: architecture - an edit to the context map itself

title: README says the pairing PIN rotates; it is fixed per launch
body:
## Summary
README.md:42 promises "Pairing QR + rotating PIN"; the PIN is drawn once per Session and never changes while the app runs.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:78 `val pin: String = (1000..9999).random().toString()` - a val, set once. Nothing in core or tv-app rotates it (grep "rotat" in core and tv-app sources: 0 hits). A stale capability claim is worse than silence: a reader would assume an exposed PIN expires. Fix: say "a PIN per launch" (or rotate it, which is a feature). README.md is outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- read README.md:42
- grep the sources for rotation
- none exists

## Expected impact
The doc stops promising a security property the product does not have.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the README states the PIN lifetime the code has
Before: 1 false capability claim
After: 0
Method: probe - README line vs Session.kt and a grep for rotation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
README.md:42 `- Pairing QR + rotating PIN; a phone with the wrong PIN is refused.`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:78 `val pin: String = (1000..9999).random().toString()`
instrument: out-of-scope (README.md): a doc edit checked by grep that no "rotating" claim remains unless a rotation test exists

title: The wrong-PIN limit is a lockout, which the pairing standard calls a DoS lever
body:
## Summary
device-pairing / timing-defenses prefers a fixed delay on every failed attempt over a lockout table, because a lockout keyed on attacker-suppliable input lets anyone lock out the legitimate holder; the pen's limit is a 5-strike, 30 s desk-wide lockout.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt PairingDesk.check locks every hello, the right PIN included, after MAX_WRONG_PINS. Since f0189837 that covers LAN connections too, so a LAN neighbour sending 5 wrong hellos every 30 s keeps the viewer from pairing indefinitely (before it, they could instead brute-force and take the pen, which is worse). The technique's answer is a fixed artificial delay before each refusal, applied uniformly, which a sans-IO core can express only as an effect the shell carries out (tv-app PenSessionHost). Parallel connections defeat a per-connection delay, so the real choice (delay, lockout, longer PIN, both) is a policy call.

## Flow
- a neighbour scripts 5 wrong hellos per 30 s
- the viewer's right PIN is refused "too many wrong PINs"
- the viewer cannot pair while the script runs

## Expected impact
Decides which attacker the pairing defends against best: the guesser (now limited) or the jammer (now enabled).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - neither guessing nor jamming the pairing is cheap
Before: jam: 5 hellos per 30 s keep pairing closed; guess: 5 per 30 s
After: unmeasurable until the policy is chosen (fixed delay needs a shell-side delay effect and a parallel-connection cap)
Method: simulation - walked through PairingDesk.check with an interleaved jammer; the rung above needs the shell change in tv-app
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
ai-registry device-pairing/techniques/timing-defenses.md "a lockout keyed on an attacker-suppliable identifier is a tool for locking out the legitimate holder"
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:68 PairingDesk.check `if (lockedUntilMs != null) return PinCheck.LOCKED`
escalation: direction - choose the throttle policy (lockout vs fixed delay vs PIN length); needs tv-app

title: The pairing PIN is 4 digits from a non-cryptographic random
body:
## Summary
Session draws the PIN with kotlin.random's default generator over 1000..9999, 9000 values, from a seed nobody chose for secrecy.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:78 `(1000..9999).random()` uses Random.Default, not SecureRandom. Registry device-pairing / pairing-ceremony asks for an entropy floor on the pairing secret. With the desk-wide limit (f0189837) an online brute force takes on average 4500 guesses at 5 per 30 s, about 7.5 h; the space itself is the remaining weakness. Fix candidate: SecureRandom, and possibly 6 digits (the PIN box already allows 8). tv-app is outside this round.

## Flow
- the TV starts; Session draws a PIN
- a guesser has 9000 candidates at 5 per 30 s

## Expected impact
Raises the cost of guessing by the PIN-space factor. 6 digits costs the viewer two more keystrokes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the pairing secret has a stated entropy floor
Before: 9000 values, non-cryptographic RNG; ~7.5 h mean brute force under the limit
After: predicted 900000 values with SecureRandom; ~750 h
Method: simulation - arithmetic over the limit constants; the change is in tv-app
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:78 `val pin: String = (1000..9999).random().toString()`
companion/index.html:83 PIN input maxlength="8"
instrument: out-of-scope (tv-app): a JVM test that the PIN source is SecureRandom-backed and its length; live-ui-test/relay-test read the PIN from logcat so they need no change

title: A "too many wrong PINs" refusal does not say when to retry
body:
## Summary
The lockout refusal carries a reason string only; the phone cannot know the cooldown ends in 30 s, so its copy hard-codes "half a minute".

## Description
TvMessage.Welcome (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:107) has sessionId, videoAspect, accepted, reason. Registry rate-limiting / refusal-contract: a refusal tells its caller when a retry can succeed. PairingDesk knows lockedUntilMs. Fix candidate: an optional retryAfterMs on Welcome (encodeDefaults with explicitNulls=false keeps old phones decoding), set on LOCKED; the page counts down and enables Pair then. In-tree contract (core + companion), verifier: CompanionContractTest + companion-refusal-test.

## Flow
- a phone is refused "too many wrong PINs" 10 s into a cooldown
- the page says wait half a minute
- the viewer waits 30 s when 20 would do, or retries early and is refused

## Expected impact
The viewer retries at the right moment. Additive field; older pages ignore it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the locked phone knows when to retry
Before: retry time on the wire: none; page copy fixed at "half a minute"
After: predicted: exact remaining ms on the wire, page countdown
Method: simulation - walked through PairingDesk.check and the page; no test pins the field yet
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:107 `data class Welcome(val sessionId: String, val videoAspect: Double, val accepted: Boolean, val reason: String? = null)`
companion/index.html locked copy "wait half a minute, then type the PIN" (f040d7c7)
instrument: PairingGuessLimitTest case: LOCKED Welcome carries retryAfterMs = lockedUntil - now; companion-refusal-test case: the fake TV sends it and the page shows the countdown

title: Messages the engine drops leave no trace
body:
## Summary
PenEngine now drops a malformed shape, a short point and a shape tap silently; the conversation reports undecodable frames to the shell, but nothing counts what decoded and was dropped.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt routes undecodable frames to onUndecodable (logged by tv-app). PenEngine.handleShape / handlePen (core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt) return early without a record since f85c84ca and 701bf033, and unknown tools and phases were already dropped that way. When a pen "draws but nothing appears", nothing afterwards says why. Fix candidate: a dropped-message counter on PenEngine, surfaced in HealthReading / /health (tv-app Health.kt) for the harness.

## Flow
- a client sends shape tool "spot" (a typo) or a short point
- the engine drops it
- GET /health shows annotations unchanged and no reason

## Expected impact
The harness and a debugging operator can tell "never arrived" from "arrived and dropped". Adds one field to the /health body.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a dropped pen message is countable after the fact
Before: 0 records of dropped decoded messages
After: predicted: a counter in /health per drop reason
Method: simulation - three drop paths walked; surfacing needs tv-app Health.kt
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt handleShape `else -> null` and the early returns
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HealthBody.kt:13 HealthReading has no drop count
instrument: HealthBodyTest case for the new field plus a PenEngine test that each drop path bumps the counter; tv-app Health.kt wiring is out-of-scope
